findings.location: design.md §"The UI panel" code sketch — <HelpPopover concept="career-advancement">
findings.problem: The HelpPopover pseudocode omits children, but HelpPopoverProps.children is required (children: string). Every real call site passes text, e.g. AdvancementPlanner uses {getHelpContent('career-advancement')}. As written the sketch would not compile.
findings.fix: Match the planner exactly: <HelpPopover concept="career-advancement">{getHelpContent('career-advancement')}</HelpPopover>, importing getHelpContent from ../../logic/help-content. The 'career-advancement' concept already exists in help-content.ts.

findings.location: design.md §"The goal model" / §"The UI panel" target-level selector
findings.problem: "level titles (getCareerLevelOptions)" is imprecise: getCareerLevelOptions(careerName) returns CareerLevel[] objects, not title strings.
findings.fix: State the selector maps getCareerLevelOptions(targetCareer).map(l => l.title) for labels and tracks the 1-based level number for goal.level, so a CareerLevel object is not passed where a number/string is expected.

findings.location: design.md §"The pure engine" careerLevel multi-level climb, projection step 3
findings.problem: The projection is described as setting the clone's career/careerLevel/class, but the new planLevelRequirements(character, careerName, levelNum) resolves the level by levelNum and derives the threshold internally — it never reads the clone's careerLevel title. Mutating careerLevel on the clone is dead work and could imply title-resolution is in play (it is not for the extracted helper).
findings.fix: Clarify that only the projected advance counts (chars .a, skill rows, talents) matter; planLevelRequirements is called with an explicit levelNum, so the clone's career/careerLevel/class need not be touched and touching them has no costing effect.
